frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The forcible propulsion of hard projectiles at a target — a directed hurling/pelting whose function is to strike, batter, and thereby drive off, expel, or bring down that target.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The forcible propulsion of hard projectiles at a target — a directed hurling/pelting whose function is to strike, batter, and thereby drive off, expel, or bring down that target.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across every occurrence the root contributes the image of pelting: hard objects hurled AT a target to strike and repel it. (1) The finite verbs are all literal stoning threats — "we would have stoned you" (11:91 لَرَجَمْنَٰكَ), "they will stone you" (18:20 يَرْجُمُوكُمْ), "I will surely stone you" (19:46 لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ), "we will surely stone you" (36:18 لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ), "that you stone me" (44:20 تَرْجُمُونِ). Here the pelting-to-drive-off/kill is on the surface. (2) The passive participle marjūmīn (26:116, "you will be among the pelted ones") is the same act viewed from the target. (3) rujūm (67:5) names the projectiles themselves: the sky's lamps are "made rujūm FOR the devils" — objects hurled to drive off the shayāṭīn; this verse is the internal keystone tying the projectile sense to the shayṭān. (4) The epithet rajīm — Iblīs told "you are rajīm" then expelled (15:34, 38:77), and "the rajīm Satan" (15:17, 16:98, 3:36, 81:25) — is exactly the passive "pelted/driven-off, hence outcast" one, bridged internally by 67:5's rujūm-for-devils. (5) rajm bi-l-ghayb (18:22, guessing the sleepers' number) is the same hurl-at-a-target act with the target unseen: casting conjecture blindly "at the hidden." Subtracting form, construction, participants and context, the invariant left is: cast hard things at a target to strike and drive it away.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: verb I = to perform the pelting (11:91, 18:20, 19:46, 36:18, 44:20); verbal noun rajm = the act/instance of pelting, here abstracted to a mode of speaking (18:22); noun plural rujūm = the hurled projectiles (67:5); passive participle marjūm = the pelted target (26:116); the intensive/passive adjective rajīm = "one pelted and so driven off/outcast" (6 Satan occurrences). CONSTRUCTION: the bi-l-ghayb frame in 18:22 re-vectors the hurl toward an invisible target (= baseless conjecture); the li-(dative) frame in 67:5 (rujūman li-l-shayāṭīn) marks the projectiles as ordnance FOR pelting devils; direct-object/accusative frames on the verbs supply the human victim. PARTICIPANTS: hostile crowds vs. prophets (Shuʿayb, Ibrāhīm's father, Nūḥ's people, the townsfolk, Pharaoh's people), God vs. Satan, cosmic lamps vs. devils — none of these is the residue. CONTEXT: legal-threat/mob-violence, narrative expulsion of Iblīs, cosmology of the guarded heaven, polemic on conjecture — all stripped. Residue after subtraction = hurl-hard-projectile-at-a-target-to-strike-and-drive-off.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 18:22 رَجْمًۢا بِٱلْغَيْبِ ("rajm at the unseen," i.e. guessing the number of the Sleepers). It contains no stones and no expulsion, so it looks like a pure speech-act. It reconciles because the root still supplies the throwing/casting act: the speakers are hurling assertions AT a target they cannot see, so the projectile is verbal and the "unseen" is the missing target — the very feature (blind, aimless casting) that distinguishes it from informed speech. The construction bi-l-ghayb, not the root, adds "at the hidden"; strip it and the recoverable residue is still "casting [something] at [a target]." A close runner-up is the rajīm epithet (e.g. 15:34, 3:36): on the surface it reads as static "accursed/outcast," but 67:5 supplies the internal bridge — devils are the standing objects of rujūm (hurled projectiles) — so rajīm = "the pelted-and-thereby-driven-off one," not an unrelated sense of cursing.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative core is "expel / drive away / render outcast (curse)." It fits the six rajīm-Satan occurrences and the expulsion of Iblīs elegantly, and it can gloss the stoning verbs as "drive off by stones." Internal evidence arbitrates AGAINST making expulsion the residue: (a) 67:5 rujūm are concrete physical MISSILES, not acts of expulsion — the projectile/hurling notion is primary and the driving-off is its effect; (b) 18:22 rajm bi-l-ghayb involves no expulsion at all, only casting/throwing (of conjecture); (c) 26:116 al-marjūmīn foregrounds being pelted, with expulsion only entailed. Because "hurl projectiles at a target" generates the expulsion, the outcast-status, AND the conjecture reading, while "expel/curse" fails to generate the physical missiles and the aimless-casting sense, the pelting core is the deeper invariant and expulsion is a downstream entailment.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) qdhf (قذف) — generic casting/hurling (of stones, or into fire, or of slanderous accusation); rjm is narrower: pelting specifically with hard projectiles (stones/missiles) so as to strike-and-drive-off a target. (2) rmy (رمي) — throwing/shooting, including archery and neutral tossing; rjm lacks the ballistic-aim/marksmanship nuance and instead carries the battering, driving-away, repelling entailment (hence its projectile plural rujūm and its outcast epithet rajīm). (3) lʿn / ṭrd (لعن / طرد) — verbal cursing / driving away from mercy; rjm overlaps in the "outcast" result but its distinctive mechanism is the physical pelting (67:5), not a spoken curse. Falsifiability: the pelting core is refuted if any occurrence uses rjm for expulsion or cursing with (a) no throwing/casting event on the surface AND (b) no internal projectile bridge — pure verbal denunciation labelled rjm would break it. No occurrence does this; even the rajīm epithet is anchored by 67:5's rujūm.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — "hurl hard projectiles at a target to strike and drive it off" — is recoverable in all 14 occurrences without forcing. It is directly on the surface in the five stoning verbs (11:91, 18:20, 19:46, 36:18, 44:20), in the pelted-target participle (26:116), and in the projectile plural rujūm (67:5). Two families require internally-attested metaphorical extension rather than surface reading: the six rajīm-Satan epithets (15:17, 15:34, 16:98, 38:77, 3:36, 81:25), read as "pelted-and-driven-off = outcast" and bridged by 67:5 where devils are the explicit objects of rujūm; and rajm bi-l-ghayb (18:22), read as casting conjecture blindly at an unseen target. Because those two families depend on an inference (a determinate one, with the direction fixed by 67:5) rather than a surface pelting event, the unity is robust but not surface-recoverable everywhere, and the root's boundary with qdhf/rmy is real but not razor-sharp — hence MODERATE rather than STRONG. No occurrence contradicts the residue, so inconsistent_refs is empty and clean presence across all 14 is claimed on the basis of the attested bridge, not by suppressing an anomaly.

adversarial_verification.notes: Refutation sweep, 14/14 accounted for. STRONG CORE: the five finite verbs (11:91, 18:20, 19:46, 36:18, 44:20), the passive participle marjumin (26:116), and rujum (67:5) all directly instantiate the frozen candidate — hard projectiles hurled at a target to strike/kill/drive off. 67:5 (lamps made rujum FOR the shayatin) is a genuine, non-circular textual keystone that also props up the rajim epithets. HARDEST CASE #1 — the rajim epithet cluster (15:17, 15:34, 16:98, 38:77, 3:36, 81:25): classical lexica frequently gloss رجيم as ملعون/مطرود (accursed/driven-from-mercy), a sense reachable via l'n (curse) WITHOUT any projectile image, which threatens collapse into the neighbor root l'n and homonymy. Resolution: the candidate survives this because 15:34/38:77 pair 'you are rajim' with immediate expulsion (fa-khruj), and 67:5 concretely makes the shayatin the pelted target — so the passive 'pelted → outcast' reading is textually anchored, not merely asserted. This case is defensible, so NOT logged as failing. HARDEST CASE #2 and the one real failure — 18:22 رجماً بالغيب ('conjecturing about the unseen'): here there is no hard projectile, nothing is struck/battered, and no target is driven off/expelled. The frozen candidate's explicit FUNCTION clause ('to strike, batter, and thereby drive off, expel, or bring down that target') is genuinely ABSENT. It is saved only by reconstrual — metaphorizing 'hard projectiles → words of conjecture' and silently dropping the strike/repel function — which is precisely the over-specification the frozen wording invites. The bare invariant 'cast/hurl AT a target' does survive at 18:22, but the candidate as frozen (hard projectiles + strike/drive-off function) does not. This is an over-narrow-wording problem, not a semantic split. NEIGHBOR-ROOT CONTRAST: distinct from rmy (generic throw/shoot) and qdhf (hurl/cast, incl. into fire) by the specific image of pelting with stones to kill/expel; distinct from l'n (curse) and Trd (expel) for the verbal core, though the rajim epithet's edge against l'n is thin and rests on the 67:5 anchor. DISTINCTIVENESS_OK true (discriminates for the concrete core; weakest at the epithet). FALSIFIABLE true (clear failure condition: an occurrence with no cast-at-target notion; the candidate is not infinitely elastic). VERDICT PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED: no genuine homonymy/split exists (everything ties to throwing/casting at a target), so not REFUTED; but the frozen candidate is over-specified and its function clause genuinely fails to apply to 18:22 without reconstrual, so not fully SUPPORTED.

occurrence_dispositions.note: لَرَجَمْنَٰكَ 'we would have stoned you' — literal threat to pelt Shuʿayb with stones to kill/drive off; pelting residue on the surface.
شَيْطَٰنٍ رَّجِيمٍ — passive 'pelted/driven-off, hence outcast' devil; metaphorical extension bridged by 67:5's rujūm-for-devils logic.
فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ paired with فَٱخْرُجْ 'get out' — Iblīs declared pelted/driven-off then expelled; the drive-away function of the pelting act is explicit.
ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ — the pelted/outcast Satan; same passive rajīm epithet bridged via 67:5.
يَرْجُمُوكُمْ 'they will stone you' — literal pelting threat against the sleepers if discovered; drive-off/kill function present.
رَجْمًۢا بِٱلْغَيْبِ 'casting/hurling at the unseen' — same hurl-at-a-target act with the target (the sleepers' number) hidden; bridged by candidate's own logic of blind casting.
لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ 'I will surely stone you' — Ibrāhīm's father threatens literal pelting to drive him off; surface stoning sense.
ٱلْمَرْجُومِينَ 'the pelted ones' — passive participle, Nūḥ threatened to be among those stoned; the act viewed from the target.
لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ 'we will surely stone you' — literal pelting threat against the messengers; drive-off/harm function on the surface.
فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ with فَٱخْرُجْ — Iblīs declared pelted/outcast then expelled; parallel to 15:34, drive-away sense explicit.
ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ — the pelted/driven-off Satan sought refuge from; rajīm epithet bridged by 67:5.
أَن تَرْجُمُونِ 'that you stone me' — Mūsā seeks refuge from being pelted/stoned; literal drive-off/kill threat.
رُجُومًا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِ — the lamps 'made projectiles/missiles for the devils'; names the hurled objects themselves, the internal keystone of the projectile sense.
شَيْطَٰنٍ رَّجِيمٍ — pelted/outcast devil; passive rajīm epithet bridged via 67:5's rujūm-for-devils.
